newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.Korea's Ssangyong buys its first W.African crude.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Ssangyong buys its first W.African crude.

text.p: South Korean refiner Ssangyong Oil has bought West African crude for the first time and adding another source of demand to the growing trade, oil traders said on Thursday.
Two million barrels of Nigerian Bonny Light crude, loading in the first week of July, were purchased by the refiner from Shell, they said.
West African crudes have regularly moved into other South Korean refiners in the past two years, but this is the first time that SSangyong has purchased the regional crude.
Traders attributed the purchase to tightening specifications for fuel oil in South Korea. In July, South Korea plans to cut the sulphur content in fuel oil for urban areas in half to 0.5 percent.
Ssangyong, which has a total refining capacity of 443,000 barrels per day, is South Korea's third largest refiner.
Saudi Arabia's state-oil company Saudi Aramco owns 35 percent of the refiner and provides the bulk of Ssangyong's crude requirements.
West African crude has become a favourite import of South Korean refiners, partly because the low-sulphur crude helps compensate for the lack of desulphurisation capacity in the refining sector.
South Korea has taken the biggest proportion of West African grades in Asia so far in 1997 -- at almost 23 percent of the total.
Shipping consultants Richardson Lawrie estimated that eastbound fixings of West African crudes through May totalled 770,000 barrels per day (bpd), up 30.4 percent from the year-earlier period.
Tanker broker Simpson, Spence & Young estimated the fixings at 805,000 bpd, which by their figures was a 12.8 percent rise ont eh year.
